title: Cap. IX Arg. 9 Sol close: God creates in time those not predestined to beatitude — creation's proper end is communication of good, not damnation as intended scope
pass_a_gloss: God therefore creates in time those whom from eternity he by no means predestined unto beatitude, whom he foresaw by their own fault about to rush unto voluntary destruction, whom he decreed to permit that they should fall into this everlasting misery: but meanwhile the creation of men (which in the order of decreeing preceded all these things) had its own proper end, the glory of God in the diffusion and communication of good, not their damnation, which is to be held an event following the creation of the reprobate, not a scope intended by God creating.
pass_b_english: So God creates in time those he from eternity did not predestine to beatitude — whom he foresaw would by their own fault rush to voluntary ruin, whom he decreed to permit to fall into this everlasting misery. Yet men's creation (which in the order of decreeing preceded all that) had its own proper end: God's glory in the diffusion and communication of good — not their damnation, which is to be held an event following the creation of the reprobate, not a scope intended by God as creator.
source_text: Creat ergo Deus in tempore, quos ab aeterno minime praedestinavit ad beatitudinem, quos praevidit sua culpa ad interitum ruituros voluntarium, quos decrevit permittere ut inciderent in hanc miseriam sempiternam: sed interim creatio hominum (quae ordine decernendi haec omnia praecessit) habuit proprium suum finem, Dei gloriam in diffusione ac communicatione boni, non damnationem eorundem, quae habenda est eventus consequens creationem reprobatorum, non scopus intentus a Deo creante.
